title: The World Contract (C1) — world.json
description: One derived, language-neutral symbol artifact per project. Two flat tables: the symbols each court declares, and the references between them. Governed by contracts/world-contract.md v1.0; the two files move together.

world.description: The project this world belongs to.

contract.description: The World Contract version this artifact was emitted against. MAJOR.MINOR.

generated.description: Optional emission timestamp, ISO 8601. Informational: staleness is the build's problem, not the reader's.

name.description: A symbol name in its declaring language. No space, no newline (stzGraph node-id rule). Dots qualify a field: deposit.amount.

symbolKind.description: Closed set, v1.0. The first eight are the reference design's; element and state were added for StzZui's shipped verifier, whose Level-3 checks read entities, actors, state and elements.

refKind.description: Closed set, v1.0. A court emits the most specific kind it can prove; 'references' is the weakest true statement, never an escape hatch.

symbolId.description: kind:name — the C2 cite form (rule:79), reused rather than invented. Matched case-insensitively.

span.description: C2's span, verbatim — including line 0 meaning the finding is file-wide. span.file IS the declaring artifact; C1 carries no separate artifact field.

type.description: The declared type where the kind has one — a field's type, a flow's return. Null or absent otherwise.

rationale.description: The declaration's own RATIONALE, carried verbatim. Never normative, never compared.

ref.description: One reference SITE. The same pair referenced from three places is three rows — which is why refs is a table and not a field on the symbol.

span.description: Where the REFERENCE appears — not where either symbol is declared.
